title: מטול הברק

spec.palette: designed ramps, at most 5 steps each: steel 4, copper 3, ceramic 3, battery 2, red 3, arc 3, rubber 2, smoke 2, tag 2, mark 1

source: hand-placed pixels at 0 deg, every column (tools/art_host/weapons/arc_px.py); rows turned RotSprite-style (Scale2x x3, nearest), stray pixels out, a 1 px outline; the mark upright in the overlay only
character:
WHO: a home-made lightning gun from a roof workshop: a steel tube wound tight with copper, three white ceramic
       insulators standing on it, a plain battery strapped on top with a red terminal, and a two-pronged copper fork at
       the front that always spits a little. Nothing about anybody: just a lot of volts and some tape.
  IDLE: the fork spits small blue sparks, the insulators catch the light. CHARGE: the copper windings light up blue
        from the inside, white at full, a halo over the insulators and a crackling arc between the prongs. FIRE: a white
        flash at the fork and a short kick. OVERHEAT: the windings go red-hot and it smokes; he shakes his hand.
cell_note: a bigger cell than the contract's 64: it holds the weapon at every angle with its moving parts thrown out and the toss

equip.note: 20 ticks: up from the hip with the battery dark; at 8 it CRACKLES awake (the lamp, a spark at the fork): ready

idle.note: 1 s loop: the fork spits a small spark now and then, the windings glint once

charge.note: 48 ticks held (0.8 s): the windings light blue, at spark_1 (16) white with a halo over the insulators and an arc across the fork, at spark_2 (32) the arc leaps out in front; ready on the last frame (held until the release)

fire.note: 24 ticks: tick 0 the bolt (a white flash at the fork), a short kick back and up peaking at 2; at 8 the fork crackles as it settles: ready

overheat.note: 60 ticks: held past full it grounds through him: the windings red-hot and smoking, at 10 he SHAKES HIS HAND (it hops), then it cools: ready

empty.note: 12 ticks: the click on a flat battery (the lamp dies), a droop; at 6 he tosses it away in front of him

catch.note: the hand-off from the unarmed catch: it lands dark in his hands, the lamp comes on, the fork crackles; the reveal from the last frame

aim_note: a frame's aim = degrees the weapon turns from its rest (the idle's first frame is 0), added to the body's aim; kick = [px along the barrel (negative = back), px up, degrees up]
mark: the made-in-Israel mark as a SMALL HANGING TAG (the Host 12.11: at most 9 x 11): an ivory luggage tag with the blue outline star 7 x 7 on a 3 px cord from under the coil; upright in every row. In atlas_mark.png ONLY
mark_rect_note: per angle row, per column: [x, y, w, h] of the mark in the cell (the 9 x 11 tag, or the 11 x 11 roundel) and mark_star = the top-left pixel of the star (7 x 7 on the tag, 9 x 9 on a roundel); atlas_mark.png holds the mark alone in the same layout

events.crackle: the fork spits awake (equip 8, fire 8): a crackle
events.ready: the act is over on this frame's last tick
events.spark_1: the windings go white, the arc jumps the fork (charge 16)
events.spark_2: the arc leaps out in front (charge 32)
events.shot: the bolt (fire 0): FX's arc from `muzzle` (between the prongs)
events.click: the trigger on a flat battery (empty 0)
events.toss: the spent gun leaves his hand (empty 6)
events.reveal: RENDER fires the reveal from this pose

normal_note: by plane: every colour paints one plane of the weapon (top, front, underside ...), turned with the row; silhouette pixels face out along the edge; the upright mark faces the viewer

holds.note: THE SET'S OWN CARRY per hero body pose (the Host 12.11: a hero's face is never covered by his weapon in any pose). While the king plays one of these body animations with this weapon, draw the weapon at `aim` (degrees, the body's hand aim replaced) and its hand point moved by `offset` [x, y] px; the frame's own aim delta and kick still add. His port carry (aim 25-40) puts a long weapon across his chin and mouth; a low hip carry at -20 keeps the face and the crown clear (picture: art/weapons/host/previews/king_carry_long_weapons.png).

muzzle_note: the gap between the fork's two prong tips, per row and column: the arc starts here

glow.note: the arc's own colours as drawn in the windings and at the fork: ice blue, white core; red when overheated

cells: the canopy flat on the floor
sprites.anchor: the cell's TOP-left at `at` (frame px; the sprite stands on the cell's bottom, centred)

catch.note: the weapon's side of the unarmed set's catch, on the same ticks and hand points as the shotgun's catch.json (the body is one builder's): frames 0-2 it comes down, 3 the catch (its grip lands on the hand), 3-4 what carried it lets go, 5-6 in the hands, 7-9 held up behind his head (layer back), the reveal from 9. Its carrier is the parachute: on the catch it folds, then lies on the floor.
